title: Calcium–potassium coupling fails an incremental cross-sample resting-pulse prediction test
abstract: A source-trained calcium–potassium product did not establish incremental resting-pulse prediction across NHANES2011–2012 and2013–2014: MSE gain 0.021139bpm² (0.017%), source-targetPSU refit95% interval [-0.906140,0.425097], with slightly worse MAE. Fixed weighted ridge models with source-only preprocessing transferred from 4582 to 5021 complete-case adults. A flexible additive routine-measure comparator included total and conventionally albumin-corrected calcium. Target MSE changed 122.915885 to 122.894746bpm². Unweighted and source-percentile-clipped fits reversed the small gain. This negative incremental-model test is not equivalence or evidence against electrolyte physiology.
